key_insight: X-Lens shows that accurate metric depth can be estimated in real time from a mix of fisheye and pinhole cameras using a compact feed-forward model. Its main idea is to explicitly encode camera geometry so the model can handle heterogeneous views without heavy processing.
problem_solved: The paper addresses real-time metric depth estimation when inputs come from a variable number of calibrated cameras with different projection types, especially fisheye and pinhole lenses. This is challenging because their geometry differs significantly, making feature alignment and depth prediction difficult.
method: Uses a geometry-aware heterogeneous camera formulation to unify fisheye and pinhole views.
Introduces learnable calibration tokens to provide coarse alignment between different projective spaces.
Injects a Jacobian-parameterized distortion bias into cross-attention to model local projection changes more accurately.
impact: This matters for AI/ML practitioners because it enables practical real-time depth estimation in multi-camera systems without requiring a fixed camera layout. It is especially useful for robotics, autonomous systems, and perception pipelines that must work with mixed lens types efficiently.

paper_title: X-Lens: Real-Time Metric Depth Estimation with Heterogeneous Cameras
paper_authors: Heng Zhou, Shuhong Liu, Yonghao He, Bohao Zhang, Fa Fu
